New dredging plant generally, $60,000.
That is all over the Dominion.
Is that for repairs or building over or what ? It is hardly a new dredging plant ?

This is not so much for the building of dredges as for the building of vessels accessory to dredges, such as scows, &c. Accidents often happen, and it is from this vote that all of that is taken. Everything that is necessary as accessory to the dredges.
Dredging, 'Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island, $115,000.
This is for the running expenses of the plant belonging to the government in the maritime provinces.

Last year the Hon. Mr. Sutherland made a promise that at the first favourable opportunity when dredges could be secured some of the harbours in Halifax county would be favoured with a visit from one of those dredges. There are several public wharfs in Halifax county which require a small amount of dredging to make them effective, not a large amount but a small amount, and I would ask the minister if he would give us an engagement that at the very earliest opportunity, say next summer, he will endeavour to assist these harbours in that way. The dredging required is not extensive and a small amount would make these harbours effective.

I can only say that the large dredge ' The Fielding ' which is now being constructed- at Sorel, as soon as she is completed will greatly relieve the situation. She is very large and powerful, supposed to be the most powerful dredge in the world. When she is ready the department will have better and greater opportunities of performing works such as the hon. gentleman refers to. There has been a great deal of difficulty in the maritime provinces, the amount of dredging required is very great and in some harbours it is almost continuous, so that the Department of Public Works have considerable difficulty at all times ' in securing sufficient dredges. I can only promise to give every consideration possible to Halifax.
May I ask the hon. minister when that will be ?
I have already answered that question.
We have been promised that dredge in the province of Nova Scotia for the last three or four years.

The promise to which the hon. member for Victoria has referred I think is one that is in his memory with relation to the county of Lunenburg. The member for that county has been applying for years and nothing has been done. The promise has always been made that the dredge would be completed, and that when she was in service Lunenburg would be recognized the first of all. The general trade of tiie place is being interfered with for the want of this improvement. There is no countv that requires the dredge more than the county 1 have the honour to represent. There is more shipping there than in any other part of the province, Halifax not excepted.

I may say in connection with the observations of the minister that in Halifax county we do not require a large amount of dredging, but if we had one of the small dredges at an early period, she could do a large amount of work that would be of great benefit.

I did not intend to say that it was not the intention of the department to have the 1 Fielding ' do the work to which he refers, because I hope that she will soon be able to take the place of some of the other dredges.
I would like to know if any dredging is being done on the St. John river in New Brunswick.

There is some being done at the present time in St. John. Representations have been made to the department with regard to dredging the St. John river, and we are endeavouring to do our best to meet the wishes of the people of that river. The dredge ' New Brunswick ' is now at

*work there, where there are a number of wharfs that require a small amount of dredging. I cannot tell at which particular wharf she is working at the present time, but she is engaged doing work that has been asked for by the Navigation-Company and by the people of the city.

There are a number of dredges employed in the province of Nova Scotia doing work that is less needed than that I referred to a moment ago. A small dredge will do for some of these harbours equally as well as a larger one. I would urge that this work be looked after at the earliest possible moment, as the trade and interests of Lunenburg as a county are suffering. A number of vessels are compelled to go to Halifax and discharge there and then reship their cargoes of salt, for the want of dredging in the harbours of Lunenburg, Bridgewater and Mahone Bay.

I am sorry that I cannot make the hon. gentleman any definite promise in regard to the matter. As a matter of fact there are two dredges doing work in Nova Scotia. When we have the dredge ' Fielding ' at our disposal, we hope to relieve these dredges that are now there from some of the work they are doing, and then we shall be glad to send them somewhere else.
Why should favour be shown to those counties where the work is less needed than in my county ?
I do not think the people of those counties where these dredges are working would agree with the hon. gentleman that his county needs the work more than theirs do.
It can easily be ascertained that there is very little shipping in some places where the dredges have been employed for the last few years.
What has been the experience with the new suction dredge that was built, I mean the 1 Tarte ? '

She was only working for a short period before meeting with an accident, but the report of the engineers' department is that just previous to the accident she was doing more work than had ever been performed by any other dredge in the world. That is a large statement, but it is borne out by the reports.
What happened to her ?
Her boiler burst. But before the accident she did 38,000 yards in one day. That is entirely beyond anything that has been accomplished before.
All the more reason why she should be employed in the work I have referred to.
I am afraid the * Tarte ' would be found an unwieldy dredge to take down to Lunenburg. It is a suction dredge.

We would be well satisfied to have her there until the other can be brought into service.
Dredging, Ontario and Quebec, $95,000.
Perhaps the hon. gentleman would give us an explanation about the Port Credit harbour that I brought up.

I cannot give any more explanation than I endeavoured to give a short time ago. The hon. gentleman has applied for a certain work to be done in Port Credit harbour. Is the dredging to be done at the mouth of the harbour ?
Yes.
If it is dredging at the mouth of the harbour, the work is so small that it would be useless to give it out by contract.

Is that likely to be done this summer or fall ? I do not wish to press the matter, I understand the hon. gentleman is doing his best. It is a long time since the promise was made, but I suppose it is almost impossible for him to meet the wishes of the people at all the harbours. With regard to its being a private harbour, it is owned by a private company. But the hon. gentleman must bear in mind that the government has expended money on that harbour in days gone by. In 1892, dredginsr was done there by the department that cost $1,214.75 ; in 1893 the work cost $592. Last year the minister sent an acting engineer to examine the work, and he reported what was required in the way of repairs :
The following is an estimate of work required :-
West side, 275 lineal feet of close pile
work at $15 per	foot	 $4,125
East side, 390 lineal feet of close pile
work at $15 per	foot	 5,850
Dredging, 14,000 cubic yards at 15 cents
per yard	 2,100
General repairs to piers	 1,000

The hon. minister will notice that there was an estimate of $2,100 for dredging a small proportion of the whole amount required. I would like to draw the hon. gentleman's attention to the fact that this Is an important harbour. It is a natural harbour, there is a great deal of traffic between Toronto and Hamilton and this harbour is necessary as a harbour of refuge. I would further draw his attention to the fact that there are two large manufacturing establishments at this place, one large starch work employing a great many hands and another, a pressed brick work, which is now in operation and which is likely to employ an increased number of hands. In addition I may say, that the appropriation, if properly expended, would serve very many other citizens in that locality in respect to getting in coal supplies, a commodity which is very impor-

tant In tlie province of Ontario at the present time. If that harbour were put in proper shape vessels could come in with coal and the farmers and citizens generally in that neighbourhood would be able to purchase their coal at a very much cheaper rate than they can now, being compelled to bring it in by rail. I do not wish to press the matter further. I have introduced it at every session during this parliament. The government, I think, have made an effort in the shape of promises and I am quite sure the promises have been honestly made but there does seem to be a difficulty in securing sufficient dredges to meet a case of this kind. May I ask the hon. minister if he has a dredge working in the harbour of Toronto or of Hamilton ?
There is no dredge working at Toronto but there is a dredge engaged in some large work in Hamilton.

May we expect that possibly during this summer something will be done ? I may say that the longer the delay the greater will be the work that will be necessary. In the petition that was presented to the government from this section last year it was pointed out that:
The entrance to the harbour is almost filled with sand, making it impossible for vessels with a draught of 4 or 5 feet to enter. I
I would therefore draw the attention of the hon. minister to the fact that the longer the delay the greater will be the amount of work'necessary, and that possibly the estimate given by the engineer last year of $2,100, if the work is left for another year, will require to be doubled. The hon. minister will see the importance of securing a dredge as soon as possible in order that the citizens of that section of the country may be served by a proper appropriation for the prosecution of this work.

The petition to which the hon. gentleman refers was brought to the attention of the department and there have been numerous requests made in regard to this work which the hon. gentleman has so forcibly brought to the attention of the committee. It will be the duty of the department to give its attention to the matter, but in the absence of any available dredge it is entirely impossible for me to make such a promise as he suggests. I can only hope that circumstances will intervene that will permit this dredging to be done.
Do I understand that as soon as this dredge is available the hon. gentleman will give it his attention ?

As soon as the dredge is available I will give it my serious attention.
Dredging, British Columbia, $35,000.

Before we leave the question of dredging in the west there is a matter that I would like to call to the attention of the hon. Minister of Public Works, as I understand the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries (Mr. Prefontaine) is to leave in a few days for British Colum-'bia. Dredging in the inner harbour of Victoria has been going on for a great many years. It is impossible to make the harbour capable of admitting the modern vessels that are coming to the port to-day, and the only port we had with sufficient water to accommodate these vessels has been taken over by the admiralty so that it has been left to a private individual to give us all the accommodation there is at the present time outside of the inner harbour for deep water vessels. That gentleman has spent half a million dollars but it has been found that the harbour which he has provided is not capable of accommodating the shipping which comes to the port. There has been a question discussed with regard to affording all the capacity that we require in the future by. the building of a breakwater from the outer point or wharf to Brotchie Ledge. It is a question that ought to have been taken up some years ago as it is the only proposition within reasonable cost that would afford the extent of harbour that is required. I think there is a distance of about a thousand yards from the shore to Brotchie Ledge, which if connected by a breakwater would afford wharfage accommodation for any amount of shipping. I would ask the hon. minister to be kind enough to call the attention of his colleague, the Minister of Marine and Fisheries. now that he is going to 'pay a visit to British Columbia, to tne matter, and ask him to look into it and report as to the feasibility of that scheme. It would cost very little to get a report upon the expense of construction from the engineer there because a very late and very close hydrographic survey has been made by Mr. Gamble, who was formerly the Dor minion engineer in British Columbia, and all the data required to have an estimate made of the cost is obtainable without any expense whatever. If the hon. minister will be kind enough to have the attention of the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries called to that matter before he goes and if Jhe will ask him to look into it while he is there it will be less expensive than if it were done at any other time.

I shall be very glad to call the attention of my colleague, the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries to the matter and ask him to look into it when he is visiting Victoria and I shall be very glad to get from him any report that he sees fit to make on his return. I am sure that if the hon. Minister of Marine and Fisheries enjoys his visit to Victoria as much as I did the last time I was there and if he

7891
receives ail the courtesies with which I was ifavoured he will come back in a happy frame of mincl and will be able to recommend to the department any expenditure that may be required to have the work done.
Public Works, slides and booms, St. Maurice district-improvements of boom works to facilitate the floating and storage of logs, &c., $40,000.

This is a revote. The intention is to proceed with the work of the construction of mooring piers and fly booms, the construction of a mooring pier at Ste. Flore, the construction of 600 feet of two fly booms at Les Hetres, the construction of a mooring pier at Pointe & Bernard and other works and in addition to these there are the usual contingencies amounting in all to $40,000.
I would like to ask the hon. minister if he knows what it costs the government to meet the running expenses of these booms and slides and what the revenue from them is ?
The gross revenue was $29,232 and the cost of running expenses $11,501, apart from construction charged to capital.

In this case the government gets a surplus of revenue over expenditure which in most instances is not the case. I do not see why the government should go into the business of erecting booms and slides for lumbermen. I have been in the business for thirty years and whenever there was a boom or slide or dam to be built I did it myself. The government might as well build sawmills for the lumbermen.

This question has received the consideration of all governments since 1851 and it has been looked upon as a national expenditure. The revenue which is derived from it at the present time is very large. For the reason that this is a general work and that one individual for lack of capital or other reasons could not undertake it, it is undertaken by the government.
Roads and bridges.-To open a pack trail from Peace River to Pelly River, $25,000.

This Is asked for by the mounted police, the intention being to open a trail so that in case of emergency, police might be sent from British Columbia to the Yukon.
Telegraph line between Deer Island, New Brunswick, and Eastport, Maine, $3,500.
Is it the intention of the government to build that line this year Y
Yes.
How many miles of government lines in Canada ?
Six thousand five hundred.
Is Prince Edward Island connected with the government telegraph system ?
No. I have a map here of all our telegraph lines which I will send to the hon. gentleman.
Thank .you. Is it the intention to extend the Magdalen Island line to Cape Breton ?
It is now connected in an indirect way by iSt. Paul's island and is open for private business.
How near does the line approach Prince Edward Island ?
The nearest point is Port Hood, a distance of about thirty miles.
What would it cost to extend that line to Prince Edward Island?
From $600 to $700 a knot.
That would be about $20,000. What rates do you charge ?
They are based upon commercial rates.

On a recent visit to Prince Edward Island, I found there was a great deal of dissatisfaction in regard to the existing telegraph service. The rates paid by the people are double the ordinary rates and from eight o'clock at night till eight o'clock in the morning telegraph communication with the rest of the world is cut off. Has the government under consideration the amelioration of the telegraphic conditions in Prince Edward Island, which apparently could he effected by a small expenditure in connecting the island with the government system at Port Hood ? That may be a suggestion which is impracticable. 1 am asking entirely for Information.

The matter has been brought to the attention of the department, and there is an item in the supplementary estimates of $5,000, in addition to the $2,000, .which was the amount in the estimates last year. I intend to ask the House to place that $5,000 at the disposal of the department, so that it may enter into negotiations with the companies with a view to obtaining an improved service for Prince Edward Island. That is the idea with which the amount is placed in the estimates. Whether it would prove a profitable undertaking for the government to construct the cable line, which the hon. gentleman suggests, is a matter that would have to be considered.
No disposition was made of the sum voted last year ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
That is a sum voted annually, arising out of the terms of union, which require that we shall keep up telegraphic communication with Prince Edward

Island ; and the $2,000 a year is an old subsidy which the Dominion government was to pay. It is now proposed to increase the vote from $2,000 to $7,000, in the hope that we may come to a better arrangement with the companies. With regard to a cable between Port Hood and the island, that would hardly improve the communication in the way the island people most desire. What they are anxious to have is communication with the mainland and also with all parts of the upper provinces ; and the hope is that some arrangement may be made with the present companies whereby, in consideration of some increased subsidy, they will reduce the rates and give the accommodation which the people require in regard to later hours.
IiOEDEN. If you connect the island with Port Hood, would you not connect it with the telegraph system of Nova Scotia, and therefore with that of the continent ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Yes ; hut there is not much commercial business coming from the upper provinces by that way. I think all the commercial business would come by the Western Union or the Canadian Pacific Railway lines. However, all these matters are worthy of consideration. We ail recognize the desirability of giving the island better accommodation, and if the House votes the minister the $5,000 which he is asking for, we hope that some arrangement can be made with the companies. If not, the question of the advisability of the government laying a cable will arise. [DOT] That could best be done between the capes, and perhaps some working arrangement could be made with the companies.
Communication between the island and Port Hood would connect with the Western Union system. I do not know whether the Canadian Pacific Railway lines extend there or not.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: They are not in that part of Cape Breton.

I recollect that there is some difference between the view of the contract with this cable company held by the people of the island and the view of those interested in the company. I do not remember the exact nature of the dispute. Possibly the Minister of Finance will recall it.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: Yes. The original contract with the company, which was first known as the New York, Newfoundland and London Telegraph Company, which has, since been absorbed or controlled by the Anglo-American, which is associated with the Western Union Company, provided that no other company should have the right to land a cable on Prince Edward Island. But from the point of view of the Island people, and the point of view of the Canadian government, that is understood to apply entirely to the landing of a cable from Europe, and would not shut out the landing of a cable from Canada. The company takes a different view ; but the parliament of Canada has rejected that view in the last year or two by granting a charter to another cable company, giving it the right to do business with Prince Edward Island, as well as with other parts of Canada. The question may possibly have to be decided in the courts ; but the idea of the monopoly has never been acknowledged by the government of Canada.

I am glad that the matter lias received the attention of the government. There will be an opportunity of discussing it again. May I ask the Minister of Public Works whether the extension of the government system of telegraphs is in pursuance of any definite plan, or whether it is made from time to time as immediate circumstances may seem to require ?

I do not think there is any definite plan. Each case is considered
as it comes up.
That was not the statement made a couple of years ago. We were told that there was a definite plan, and that the government telegraph system was being extended from time to time along the coast.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The general rule with regard to the government telegraph lines is that they shall be extended to portions of the coast which are isolated-in other words, to portions of Canada which ordinary commercial enterprise would hardly reach. That is the idea with which they were started, and we still cling to that idea. In pursuance of it. we are opening up the Yukon and the Labrador coast by telegraph. In a sparsely settled country there may be reasons, in the saving of life and property, for erecting telegraph lines.
For example, between Port Hawkesbury and Port Hood there is a land line indicated. Is there a private line between these two points ?

There is, I understand, a private line between those two points-the main line of the Western Union.
Telegraph lines-Quebec-Bersimis to God-bout telegraph line, P. Q., $6,000.
What is the distance from Bersimis to Godbout ?
About 90 miles.
Is there a drive road or sleigh road between these points ?

This is being built along the shore.
Telegraph lines-Quebec-to repair and improve roadway and increase operating facilities generally to eastward of .Godbout, $1,000.

Is not that a provincial
work ?

This is for the roadway on either side of the line for the purpose of the maintenance of the line and is not a highway.
Telegraph lines-Quebec-Anticosti island- renewal of line wire between Fox Bay and Becseie River, $3,000.
How is the Marconi system, to which we are giving $80,000 per year, working ?

Very satisfactorily, but this is a matter which comes under the Marine and Fisheries Department.
Miscellaneous-Public Works, arbitrations and awards, including payments authorized, notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Civil Service Act, $5,000.
Is it because you are expecting to employ civil servants as arbitrators and pay them something in addition to their salaries that you put in this item ?

The expenditure last year on this vote was only $226.12. The vote is only taken in case any expenditure should be necessary.
Public Works-miscellaneous-surveys and inspections, $50,000.
You spent $50,000 last year. What was that for ?

It was spent on purchasing instruments and supplies necessary for surveys. The season was too late last year to start the survey, but the supplies were purchased and the parties are out in the field now.
How many is the party to consist of ?

Each party consists of ten or twelve-the ordinary survey party.
National Art Gallery, Ottawa, including the purchase of painting on the advice of a committee of artists, $7,500.

With the consent of the House $750 of this will be spent in having a painting of the late Chief Justice Armour.
Public Works Department-Chief Architect's office-salaries of architects, draughtsmen and clerks, notwithstanding anything in the Civil Service Act, $32,200.
Why do you put these \\ ords in ' notwithstanding anything in the Civil Service Act ? '

Because these are technical men, not put on the permanent list, and you could not get the services of such men if they had to come in for the small sum of $400.
Public Works Department-miscellaneous- to provide for one half of the salary of the departmental photographer, $800.

,
Mr. SPROuLE. In connection with this vote I would ask why it is that after the adoption of the amendment of last year providing for the placing of these temporary clerks upon the permanent list we still provide the same vote for the same number of employees.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: The amendment of last year did not require that all these persons should not be put on the permanent list. It was an enabling Act which enabled the government to take a number of these temporary people and put them on the permanent list. It was not intended that they all should be put on but in many cases it w;ys done. It was done in many cases but not universally.
I thought that all who had been employed for a certain number of years were placed on the permanent list V

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
The intention was to take a number of the temporaries who were especially qualified and worthy and put them on the permanent list. I think in this case they were not put on.
Public Works Department-Miscellaneous- to provide for expenditure in connection with a transportation commission, $25,000.

We have no report from the Transportation Commission yet. They are visiting different parts of the country and I would suggest that they should make an annual report as they are conducting themselves as if their commission was a permanent commission.

think the non. gentleman's suggestion is a good one. There has been no final report yet and I shall communicate with the committee asking them for an interim report or a report which can be distributed with the report of the Public Works Department.
Land and cable telegraph lines, lower St. Lawrence and maritime provinces, including working expenses of vessels required for cable service, also maintenance of Marconi wireless telegraphy at Belle Isle, $80,000.
I thought this was in the Marine Department.
No. I am infornled that this part of the system is working very well and very satisfactory. It is only twenty-two miles.
This was the sum which we gave them.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext:
No, my hon. friend was mistaken. It happens to be an equal sum but the $80,000 which we gave to the Marconi Company for a station at Glace Bay is what my hon. friend is referring to. That $80,000 was a special vote that appeared only in one year. It was paid and the transaction was closed so far as our expenditure is concerned. The matter has not made

all the progress we could desire, but the Marconi people tell us that the experiments are going on satisfactorily. They have been telling us that for many months, and we are not in a position to give much additional information on the subject. This, however, is a different matter, and is for maintenance of other telegraph service.
Quebec harbour improvements, $100,000.
This is under contract.

When will it be completed ?
Mr, HYMAN. It is a large work, and the engineer informs me it will take 18 months anyway to complete it.
Is there a time fixed by the contract ?

A time is fixed by the contract, but the engineer is not prepared to say that it will be completed within the time. A great many difficulties have been met with in regard to dredging, &c., one way and another. I had the pleasure of seeing the work the other day, and I think the contractor has done very good work indeed.
Manitoba-St. Andrew's rapids improvements, Red1 river, $80,000.
What position is that work in now ?
The engineer's department is looking into the whole question, but I have not yet had any report. They were up there about a month ago.
Are you going to call for new tenders, or another contract ?

I have not yet got a report from the engineer ; when I do, I will take the matter into consideration.
Transportation facilities-lower division of Montreal harbour-improvements below St. Mary's current, $75,000.
When will this work be completed ?

Probably it will be completed this fall, this vote is to complete.
Ontario-Port Colborne-harbour improvements, $85,000.
This work is under contract, which was let on the 8th of June. 1904, and calls for completion on the 30tli of November, 1905.
Will the minister give us some explanation of the manner in which the money has been spent at Port Colborne?

All by contract. The
main breakwater has been completed. This contract is for a further eastern breakwater.
Some resolutions reported.
FIELDING (Minister of Finance) moved the adjournment of the House.
What business do you propose to take up to-morrow ?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
speechtext: I understand an lion, gentleman opposite desires to move an amendment to supply ; therefore a motion to go into supply will be made in the morning. When that motion is disposed of, the Prime Minister and the Minister of Justice will have some estimates, then the Minister of Public Works.
Motion agreed to, House adjourned at 11.55 p.m.
Friday, July 29, 1904.
